Hey all- I've been playing RPG's forever, and I just wanted to get an idea of what everyone else had played- in case I missed something really great!

My personal top ten:

  1. Suikoden II- Great mix of story, and different fight styles in a game. There's large battles where your armies clash with the Empire's, or turn-based combat between monsters and your party members. The most interesting thing is the amount of characters. I don't know the exact number- but there's well over 100 recruitable characters you can use for your party. You basically building a kingdom and castle by recruiting new characters- who then go to your little island and build your city up a bit more- unlocking more merchants etc. I loved this game.

  2. Final Fantasy 3- One of the saddest moments in my childhood was watching General Leo die in this game. While Square would renew the pain a few games later with a more important character- the hours I spent searching for a non-existent way to bring the good General back puts this one at a special spot. So many great moments- the Floating Island, the Banquet before it...the Shadow/Relm storyline... That...and Kefka was an awesome villain.

  3. Final Fantasy 7- Again, the legendary Nobuo Uematsu...the score is probably the only video game soundtrack I've ever bought. That, and Aeris' death...man...the feels. Grinding to level 99 to beat all the weapons probably contributed to my lack of a social circle during adolescence. If you haven't played the PSP Crisis Core- it develops the story a bit more.

  4. Secret of Mana- Great music, and my first crack at an action style RPG. The game was long, enjoyable, and today I still find myself whistling the theme from Potos Village every now and again.

  5. Dragon Warrior 4- This one had a chapter style approach, where you played a story for a few hours- the story would end, and you'd move on to a new character. At the end of the game the hero assembled all the character to go take on the final dungeon. The game was hard, but groundbreaking at the time- and is still playable today, in my humble opinion.

  6. Chrono Trigger- Not much needs to be said here, this game is legendary.

  7. Skyrim- I used to be an adventurer like you, until I took an arrow to the knee. Need I say more? Add in the UI and ENB enhancements and this game is probably the most gorgeous RPG out there (sorry WItcher fans.) Hundreds upon hundreds of hours of RPG goodness.

  8. Lufia 2: Rise of the Sinistrals- This was a SNES release that had a great mix of dungeon puzzles to solve, and turn based combat. The game was long, satisfying, and engaging. I definitely recommend trying it if you somehow missed it.

  9. Final Fantasy 10- While not as endearing as the two earlier favorites- this one is still a top notch RPG with graphics, music and a great story line. However, blitzball is retarded.

  10. 7th Saga- I don't know why I put this game on the list. Maybe because it's the only one here I haven't beaten. I actually hate this game. I HATE this game. Do not play this game unless you feel you've done something wrong, but don't want to go to the cops and turn yourself in. All kidding aside, this is probably one of the hardest RPG's I've ever played. If you beat this game, you have my respect.

Honorable Mentions: KOTOR, Diablo I-III, Ogre Battle, Neverwinter Nights, Sword of Vermillion, Breath of Fire 3, Fallout 3, Valkyria Chronicles, Xenoblade Chronicles, and Fable 1 + 2.

Best Villain: Handsome Jack from Borderlands 2

Best Hero: Han Solo. He’s always the best hero. Even if he’s not in these games.
